claims.text: Controlled annealing introduces nanoscale precipitates into CoCrFeNiAlₓ HEA.
Nanoscale precipitates act as nucleation centers for cooperative magnetic spin reorientation.
Nanoscale precipitates enhance local magnetic exchange interactions.
Precipitate-mediated spin reorientation and reduced domain-wall pinning enable a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
A fine, uniformly distributed precipitate structure maintains rapid heat exchange.
A fine, uniformly distributed precipitate structure maintains low magnetic hysteresis.
A fine, uniformly distributed precipitate structure maintains mechanical stability.
Standard casting followed by slow cooling typically produces a relatively homogeneous CoCrFeNiAlₓ microstructure with minimal fine precipitate formation.
Varying the duration of annealing at 800°C can systematically control and increase the nanoscale precipitate volume fraction.
The relevant nanoscale precipitates form particularly at grain or phase boundaries.
Relative to the slowly cooled baseline, optimally annealed material will have a higher magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
Relative to the slowly cooled baseline, optimally annealed material will exhibit reduced magnetic hysteresis.
Relative to the slowly cooled baseline, optimally annealed material will retain or improve its heat-exchange rate.
Relative to the slowly cooled baseline, optimally annealed material will retain or improve its mechanical stability.
The proposed behavior should hold at 300–400 K when annealing at 800°C produces fine precipitates without substantial coarsening or unwanted phase evolution.
Precipitate coarsening or phase instability may degrade mechanical properties.
